fixes.title: Unattended entry points still slewed the mount to a target whose coordinates were never set
fixes.summary: Dart's TargetCoordinatesUnsetRule only guards the GUI start path. POST /api/sequencer/start, sequencer_load_json and every resume_from_checkpoint reach the native executor without it, so a TargetHeader still at the palette default (RA 0h / Dec +0 deg) drove the mount to Pisces. Added unset_target_pointing_reason() and gated the two nodes that actually command the mount - execute_slew and execute_center - when they inherit pointing from the target (use_target_coords). Custom / mount-current coordinates are never gated. Test is exact 0.0/0.0, matching the Dart rule so the two surfaces cannot disagree about which sequences are runnable.
fixes.revert_check: Deleting the two `if config.use_target_coords { if let Some(reason) = unset_target_pointing_reason(...) }` blocks in execute_slew and execute_center: slew test FAILS with 'Mount slew did not reach target position. Expected RA=0.0000h, Dec=0.0000deg' (proving the mount WAS commanded), center test FAILS with status Success. Restored, both pass.

fixes.title: A name-addressed exposure burst filed its frames under the PREVIOUS burst's filter slot
fixes.summary: Residual half of the 'four surfaces disagree about the filter' finding. resolve_burst_filter() returned (name, config.filter_index) and expose.rs assigned each half only when Some, so a burst that names its filter but carries no index (what the Dart serializer emits when the profile has no index for that name) left ExecutionContext.current_filter_index holding the previous burst's slot. build_frame_context_for_save then stamped filter_name='L' next to filter_index=1 ('R') on the same frame, and bridge/api/imaging.rs forwards that as filter_position. Added instructions::wheel_filter_index_of() (inverse of wheel_filter_name_at) so a name-addressed burst asks the wheel which slot it landed in, and made resolve_burst_filter return a BurstFilter::Resolved{name,index} pair that expose.rs assigns as a UNIT, so an unresolvable slot is recorded as unknown instead of inheriting a wrong one.
fixes.revert_check: Two parts, each reverted separately. (a) replacing the `(Some(name), None) => { let index = wheel_filter_index_of(...) }` arm in expose.rs resolve_burst_filter with `index: None` -> name_addressed test FAILS (left: None, right: Some(0)). (b) additionally restoring the per-field `if let Some(index) = index` assignment in ExposeInstruction::execute -> both tests FAIL showing the original defect verbatim (left: Some(1), the previous burst's slot). Restored, all 78 instructions::tests pass.
fixes.caveats: Slot matching is case-insensitive and trims, so 'ha' matches a wheel slot named 'Ha'. A genuinely unmatched name (profile/device naming drift) records the name with no slot rather than guessing.

fixes.title: Every capture path that is not the TakeExposure node still wrote flats and one-shots with no FILTER card, under the synthetic 'nofilter' filename
fixes.summary: The wheel-report fallback the previous pass added lived in ExposeInstruction::execute, but the node is not the only capture path: flat_wizard/mod.rs:325 and the bridge one-shots call instructions::execute_exposure directly. Those bursts reached build_frame_context_for_save with `config.filter.or(ctx.current_filter)` and `config.filter_index.or(ctx.current_filter_index)` resolved INDEPENDENTLY, so the Flat Wizard's final flat burst got filter_name=None (no FITS FILTER card at all) and the renderer-less filename fallback rendered 'Flat_nofilter_0001.fits' while the wheel sat on a named slot -- flats that no calibration tool can match to the lights they were shot for. The independent .or() also reproduced the paired-slot defect on this path: a burst naming 'R' with no index inherited the previous burst's slot 0 ('L'). Moved BurstFilter/resolve_burst_filter out of the node into instructions.rs, added resolve_frame_filter() which flattens it against the running context, and resolved the burst's identity ONCE inside execute_exposure_with_renderer (after the wheel is commanded, so observed_wheel_filter reports where the frames are actually taken). That single (name, slot) pair is now what both the filename fallback and build_frame_context_for_save consume -- build_frame_context_for_save no longer reads config or ctx for the filter at all, so the three surfaces cannot diverge by construction.
fixes.revert_check: Two halves, reverted separately. (a) restoring `frame_ctx.filter_name = config.filter.clone().or_else(|| ctx.current_filter.clone()); frame_ctx.filter_index = config.filter_index.or(ctx.current_filter_index);` in build_frame_context_for_save -> flat_wizard test FAILS 'left: None, right: Some("R")' (no FILTER card) and direct_burst test FAILS 'left: Some(0), right: Some(1)' (R's name on L's slot). (b) restoring `let filter_label = match config.filter.as_deref()` in the renderer-less filename fallback -> flat_wizard test FAILS on the path assertion, got '/tmp/ns-direct-wheel-filter-.../untargeted_nofilter_0001.fits'. Restored, all 80 instructions::tests pass, cargo fmt --check clean.
fixes.caveats: The node path is unchanged in behaviour: expose.rs still resolves before it builds the save-path renderer, because the renderer closure captures an ExecutionContext snapshot and would otherwise render ${filter} from a stale value. There is now one precedence table (instructions::resolve_burst_filter) rather than two.

fixes.title: Every sequencer event was republished once per run started in the app launch, so one node failure raised N identical toasts and N Session Report lines
fixes.summary: Second multiplier behind the 'every node failure is listed twice' finding (the first, the disconnect-retry loop, was fixed in wave 2). api_sequencer_subscribe_events spawned TWO supervised tasks per call - sequencer_event_bridge and sequencer_decision_bridge - each taking its own receiver on the executor's broadcast channel and republishing everything onto the unified SkotiqEvent stream. sequencer_operations.dart:623 calls it at the top of every sequencerStart(), and the headless and remote entry points land on the same function, so run 2 of a night doubled every event, run 3 tripled it - failure toasts, Session Report lines and frame events alike. spawn_supervised_restart is a bare tokio::spawn with no registry, so the task name does not dedupe. Guarded both spawns behind a process-lifetime AtomicBool compare_exchange. Latching forever is safe here and I verified why rather than assuming: EXECUTOR is a OnceLock, its broadcast sender is built in SequenceExecutor::new() and never replaced, so the loops cannot see Closed before process teardown, and the supervisor already restarts them on panic. Chose the Rust guard over the Dart one because it also covers headless and remote.
fixes.revert_check: Deleting the whole `if SEQUENCER_EVENT_BRIDGES_STARTED.compare_exchange(...).is_err() { return Ok(()); }` block: test FAILS with 'left: 3, right: 1' - three subscribe calls, three live listeners on the executor event channel, i.e. every event published three times. Restored, passes; cargo fmt --check clean on both crates.
fixes.caveats: The test asserts SequenceExecutor::event_subscriber_count() (a new accessor on the executor) rather than a call counter, so it measures live listeners - the thing that actually duplicates events - not the guard's own bookkeeping. api_sequencer_subscribe_events is the only Rust caller of itself, so no other test in the bridge binary perturbs the global count.
